data.narrative:
Altos Labs is a late-stage biotech company founded by Hal Barron, Rick Klausner, and Hans Bishop that has raised $3.0B to date. The sector peer universe comprises 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 7 private peers in Biotech & Health, though none offered sufficient overlap in stage and valuation tier to support reliable peer-median triangulation.

Stage-progression analysis was the primary applicable method. Using total raised ($3.0B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage progression to the next round, this method implies a valuation of $3.6B. Public-comp anchoring, while calculable (sector P/S median of 6.6x across three biotech tickers), could not be applied due to the absence of target revenue data, which remains standard for private companies.

The triangulated valuation range is $3.1B to $4.1B, with a median point of $3.6B. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single applicable method and carries material uncertainty around future capital efficiency, clinical progress, and the timing of value-inflecting milestones typical in early-stage biotech. Given the sparse comparable set and lack of revenue or profitability metrics, investors should treat this range as indicative rather than determinative and request updated financial performance data to refine the analysis.
